title: Thermal spreader search: screen -> finite-element conduction -> Avila Core

limitations: CASE-003 is a research-only design-search specimen over a synthetic strip-heated plate; no device, enclosure, or operating envelope is represented.

The screening capability is unqualified and evaluated on a nominal basis; the finite-element capability produces an enclosure claim whose interval brackets discretisation only, under a qualification record that binds one NAFEMS benchmark reproduction as validation evidence.
The finite-element interpreter is the system Python binary, identified by digest; the finite-element package beside it is identified only by the version the result records.
integrity.notice: Package integrity checks byte identity only. It does not verify schemas, media semantics, execution receipts, signatures, qualification, practical suitability, or scientific correctness.

compiled.question: Does a candidate layered heat spreader keep the steady-state hotspot temperature on its heated face at or below the design limit for the declared strip heat flux and convective cooling, within the areal-mass and thickness limits, as established by two-dimensional finite-element conduction rather than by the one-dimensional screening estimate?
assumptions: The spreader is a two-dimensional cross-section of a plate of declared width heated by a uniform flux over a central strip of its heated face, insulated elsewhere on that face and on its lateral faces, and cooled by convection to a fixed ambient on its far face; the model is steady state.

The heated strip is 20 mm wide on a 100 mm plate at 50 kW/m2, cooled by 500 W/m2/K convection to 300 K; the 340 K hotspot, 100 kg/m2, and 40 mm limits are the case author's allocations chosen so that a thick aluminium plate passes, a copper-on-aluminium spreader passes lighter, and steel or polymer alone fails.
Material conductivities are isotropic nominal literature values; interfaces are perfect; no material, script, or interpreter is qualified.
The screening estimate is a one-dimensional series resistance that ignores lateral spreading and is evaluated on a nominal basis only; the finite-element interval brackets discretisation only.
This contract is a research-only design-search specimen and excludes every safety, qualification, or operational purpose.

Revision 2 sets the screen guide at 420 K: revision 1's 340 K guide could not be met by any design because the no-spreading estimate exceeds the true hotspot by about 80 K for every plate in the box, which made the all-PASS criterion unreachable by construction; the finite-element limit is unchanged.

requirements.statement: Screening estimate of the hotspot temperature is at or below 420 K (nominal basis; the estimate ignores spreading and is pessimistic, so this guide only excludes hopeless designs and establishes nothing).
Finite-element hotspot temperature on the heated face is at or below 340 K within its discretisation bracket.
Areal mass of the plate is at or below 100 kg per square metre.
Total plate thickness is at or below 40 mm.

entries.statement: Steady-state hotspot temperature on the heated face is at or below the design limit.
Areal mass of the plate is at or below the structural limit.
Total plate thickness is at or below the space available.
Temperature at every material interface is at or below that interface's limit.
entries.reason: No interface limit is declared for these materials; every interface is modelled as perfect and no adhesive or solder is represented, so the entry cannot be evaluated in this specimen.

entries.statement: Peak temperature during the declared transient is at or below the design limit.
entries.reason: The model is steady state; no transient is declared and no transient capability is bound.
